A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ehrlich functions, LLOME and MargE. Their main texts and appendices support a reliable comparison despite the changed title, expanded experiments and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLOME and genetic-algorithm experiments, including regret, feasibility, calibration, refinement and training-objective analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and adds LaMBO-2 comparisons, additional Ehrlich evaluations and an o1/Gemini prompting experiment.

M1.justification: The LLOME bilevel loop, PropEn formatting, refinement/filtering, temperature adjustments, MargE loss and clipped reward margin are retained. Moving Algorithm 1 and renaming its evaluation-budget variable from k to j do not change the procedure. LaMBO-2 is an added comparator, not a new LLOME component.

E1.justification: v3 evaluates LLOME mainly on 32- and 16-token Ehrlich instances, alongside a broader GA-only parameter sweep. v4 expands solver evaluation to four vocabulary/length/motif configurations and a half-quantization case, adds full-specification prompting, and briefly reports testing a Rough Mt. Fuji function. This substantially broadens the synthetic test conditions.

E2.justification: LaMBO-2 is newly evaluated in regret, diversity/feasibility and Pareto comparisons alongside the retained GA and LLOME variants. Its citation in v3 was not an evaluated comparison. REINFORCE remains an objective comparator; o1 and Gemini are evaluated separately through prompting.

E3.justification: New protocols include eight-sample prompting with the full function specification and a randomly initialized, 314K-parameter LaMBO-2 model using the same 10K GA seed evaluations and 2K evaluations per round as LLOME. v4 specifies tuning on f2 and transferring configurations across functions, and expands the Pareto aggregation. Existing LLOME model size, training epochs and oracle budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds an explicit half-quantization sensitivity experiment and extends diversity and Pareto analyses to LaMBO-2 and additional functions. Most oracle-selection, calibration, refinement, SFT/MargE scheduling and REINFORCE analyses are retained. Figure 13 drops the earlier 12K-evaluation refinement panel.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 6 defines calibration shading as mean plus or minus two standard errors. The identical plots retained in v4 Figures 5a and 14 lose this explanation. The 95% confidence-interval descriptions in Figures 11 and 12 remain. No increase in independent evaluation runs is reported.

E6.justification: v4 adds LaMBO-2 and additional-function results, plus prompting minimum regrets of 0.9375 for o1 and 0 for Gemini. The original f2 result, including MargE reaching zero regret at 24K evaluations, is retained. Pareto values change under expanded experiment coverage, not as same-setting performance gains. v3's per-round average-regret plot and 12K refinement panel are omitted.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2.3 adds a quantitative argument that uniformly sampled sequences become infeasible as length grows and explicitly requires q to divide k. The original MargE derivation and translation-invariance lemma remain. The newly displayed geometric-series equality contains an indexing error.

C1.justification: The title, abstract and contributions shift from demonstrating constrained LLM optimization against a GA to comparing generalist and specialized solvers. v4 adds claims about prompting limitations and solver tradeoffs, emphasizing LLOME's advantage on medium-difficulty functions while acknowledging comparable specialist performance on easier and harder cases.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantial interpretation of computational overhead, specialist steerability and hyperparameter sensitivity, and develops the biological motivation through binding and epistasis examples. It also warns that DPO's aggregate hypervolume is artificially favorable because some experiments terminate after generator collapse. Earlier calibration and reward-related qualifications largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7 adds LaMBO-2 architecture, eight-head ensembles, optimizer settings, hyperparameter ranges and cortex/poli-baselines implementation provenance. Appendix A.4 adds the prompting template, while Section 6.1 identifies the prompted model versions. These substantially extend reproducibility information, although the template leaves the transition matrix as a placeholder. Existing LLOME training details remain.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning against biophysical benchmarks and theoretical fitness landscapes, discussing GuacaMol, Therapeutics Data Commons, ProteinGym, FLEXS and Rough Mt. Fuji. LaMBO-2 becomes central to the generalist-versus-specialist framing. Much of the original LLM optimization and controllable-generation literature is retained in the extended related-work appendix.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the contribution narrative is reorganized. Related work moves before the method, evaluation follows it, results receive a separate section, and substantial original discussion and analysis move into the appendices.

P2.justification: v4 switches the main text to two columns, redraws the LLOME overview, adds biological illustrations, expands benchmark figures and regroups or relocates numerous existing plots. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering. Some presentation defects remain, including a clipped legend in Figure 10.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses an important weakness of v3's primarily GA-based external evaluation by adding a specialized solver under matched oracle budgets and examining difficulty-dependent performance. This supports clearer, more qualified conclusions about when LLM optimization is useful, reinforced by additional implementation detail and biological motivation. Lost calibration-band definitions, the clipped legend and the indexing error are limited regressions that do not outweigh the substantial gains in comparative evidence and interpretation.
